key_insight: PointX predicts intrinsic scene properties at 3D surface points rather than separately for each image pixel. This ties the decomposition to the physical surface, helping keep predictions consistent across viewpoints.
problem_solved: Recovering material properties, surface normals, and illumination from images is ambiguous. Pixel-based methods can assign conflicting properties to the same surface point when it appears in different views.
method: Use a multi-view transformer to encode a set of unposed images.
Query 3D surface points with a feed-forward model to predict intrinsic properties.
Represent intrinsics at the surface-point level instead of producing independent per-view pixel decompositions.
impact: Point-based prediction offers a route to more coherent multi-view scene understanding, potentially benefiting inverse rendering and material estimation. The supplied abstract is truncated, so performance gains and evaluation results cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Multiple camera views converging on one shared 3D surface point.
Pipeline diagram: unposed images → multi-view transformer → surface-point queries → intrinsic properties.
Conceptual comparison of conflicting per-view pixel predictions versus a shared point-level prediction.
Property icons for albedo, roughness, metallicity, surface normal, and irradiance.
paper_title: PointX: Multi-View Consistent Intrinsics by Querying Surface Points
paper_authors: Miguel Farinha, Sam Sartor, Iliyan Georgiev, Giuseppe Vecchio, Ronald Clark
